result_text:
I fixed the four default scoping conventions so they match the files they were meant for. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (339 run, 0 failures, 3 skipped), including a new test that covers the fix.

**Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:**
- **HTML generator rules** (pkgdown, Doxygen, meta generator): `(html|html|xhtml)` → `(html|htm|xhtml)`. This covers all three rules, so `.htm` pages now match and `.html`/`.xhtml` still do.
- **.NET `<doc>` XML rule**: path `.*/[.]xml` → `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches.
- **JavaScript `// Generated by` rule**: path `.*/[.]js` → `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches.
- **Gradle script rule**: `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` → `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

**New test:** `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java` has 9 cases. They check the new positives, the older matches that must still work (`.html` Doxygen, `.xhtml` meta, `build.gradle`), and that hand-written `.htm`, `.js` and `.xml` files stay out of the generated scope.

Nothing is committed. I also noticed `.*/[.](css|js)[.]map` in the same file has the same leading-`/[.]` pattern, so it can't match a file named like `app.js.map` at the root of a path. It is outside this task, so I left it alone.
